messages:
sarah: Quick sync — I'm proposing a concise 'version entry criteria' we can apply when deciding which model/version to add to the catalog and where to place it in the rollout queue. Need agreement on mandatory gates vs scoring.

omar: +1. Can you list the gates you have in mind? We should avoid adding too many blockers that slow onboarding for small community models.

sarah: Thinking of two layers:
1) Mandatory pass (hard gate): basic correctness (no catastrophic failures on eval set), safety check, quantization compatibility (8-bit/4-bit path validated), and a perf baseline (p95 latency under X ms for the target instance class).
2) Prioritization score (soft gate): a weighted mix of Reach / Impact / Confidence / Effort (RICE-like), plus a customer demand multiplier when a Paying Customer has committed.

li: For the perf baseline, can we make it percentile-adjusted by sequence length? Some models spike at long context.

maya: Agree. Also add 'eval delta' requirement — model must not regress user-facing metrics by more than Y% against the current default on our standard prompt set.

kevin: On the scoring: RICE is good but I prefer ICE for speed. Maybe use ICE for sprint-level triage and RICE for roadmap planning. We can also bake in cost delta (tokens cost + infra ops) as a negative factor.

omar: Operational concerns: if we approve model variants that require custom kernels, that's an ops burden. Should add a kernel-complexity flag (manual review if true).

sarah: Good point. So the mandatory gate includes a 'no custom-kernel requirement' unless there's a maintained patch and bench documentation.

li: For sequencing, propose this algorithm: filter candidates by mandatory gates -> tag any paying-customer requests -> run scoring. Within same score bucket, prefer model variants that are cheaper for us to host (lower memory footprint, quant-friendly). Also prefer models with compatible licensing.

maya: Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated (low traffic) -> monitor quality (real client prompts) for 48h -> expand to Hosted with autoscale off for first 24h -> add as routable default only after 7-day stability window. Fallback rules must be preconfigured (auto-route to next-best if latency or error spike).

kevin: Asking for a small UX touch: expose 'why this model is behind a gate' to the catalog page (short reasons). Helps customers self-serve and reduces tickets.

build-bot: CI: quant-compat-check passed for candidate m-3.2, perf-benchmark queued.

sarah: Decisions so far: (a) adopt two-layer gating (mandatory + scoring), (b) use ICE for quick triage and RICE for quarterly ranking, (c) require quant-compat and safety evals as hard gates, (d) add kernel-complexity review as an ops flag, (e) rollout cadence as maya suggested.

omar: Action items: I'll add kernel-complexity flag to model metadata and a simple checklist in the onboarding PR template. ETA EOD tomorrow.

li: I'll prepare the long-context perf test (sequence buckets) and add it to the eval harness. ETA 2 days.

maya: I'll write the catalog copy for gate reasons and a short FAQ. ETA 3 days.

sarah: Thanks. If no objections by EOD Pacific let's lock this flow and update the public onboarding doc.

kevin: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

li: fine by me.

omar: same.

sarah: Cool — closing the loop here. We'll run one candidate through to validate the process and iterate.
